mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 0.25% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises above 0.25% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) drop of more than 10% in the prior quarter signals weakening aggregate demand, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline of more than 1% in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for two consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >1% for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (year-over-year inflation) above 3% and FEDFUNDS above 2% for two months signals a dual shock of high inflation and restrictive policy, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% and FEDFUNDS > 2% for two consecutive months
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive monetary policy
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings, reflecting consumer pessimism, which reduces near-term consumption and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both PAYEMS and UNRATE above their respective 12-month averages for two months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month average and UNRATE > 12-month average for two months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between the level of housing starts (HOUST) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that higher-than-average HOUST predicts positive returns.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
